CAA and Hybe will collaborate across content, brand partnerships, sports, licensing and merchandising, using live experiences to “build new businesses and create greater opportunities for Hybe and the company's artists,” according to a release. articles.title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Re-Release Includes The Scene That Should Have Never Been Cut & New “Surprises”
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel/Sony The Spider-Man: Brand New Day re-release is coming to theaters, and it will include 10 minutes of footage that was cut from the original film. This includes one scene involving a character from Daredevil’s Netflix world that was revealed to have been shot but never aired in the original release. While she hasn't shown up […]
articles.content:
The Hollywood Reporter has revealed that the Rosario Dawson Night Nurse scene will be part of the re-release, titled Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day . This scene is supposed to take place when Punisher takes Spider-Man to the hospital, and she is the one there to help patch him up. While it seems like it was cut because it seemed out of place in the end, seeing Dawson back will make this new version something all fans will want to see.

The scene with Rosario Dawson is considered just one of several big surprises that will be added to the original movie. According to THR , the other surprises are not disclosed and likely won't be revealed until the movie is in theaters on Friday, December 4. This re-release will possibly help push Spider-Man: Brand New Day over the $1 billion mark in North America. It already ranks number one domestically all-time at $959 million and is the third-highest-grossing movie at the worldwide box office at $2.5 billion, sitting behind Avatar and Avengers: Endgame .

As for the possible other footage, the strongest possibility will be with the opening montage where Spider-Man is explaining what he had done since the end of Spider-Man: No Way Home . This scene includes comic-book-cover-accurate scenes with Spider-Man fighting Boomerang, Tarantula, Scorpion, Ramrod, and Tombstone. However, there were reportedly other villains he fought in this montage, including a hint at the Sinister Six. There is a chance that these villains could be added back into Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day . These deleted scenes won't be on the Brand New Day digital and 4K releases .

Other added possibilities include a scene that saw Spider-Man getting a vaccination in a school classroom to help kids beat their fear of needles and additional scenes with Frank Castle's Punisher, which would lead to the Night Nurse scene. There are also possible Avengers: Doomsday lead-ins, with a possible connective scene similar to what Avengers: Endgame did with its re-release earlier this year. Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters just two weeks later on December 18, so it would be the last possible tease for that movie.

articles.title: The Secret Behind Anthony Hopkins’ Hannibal Lecter Set a Bar Movies Still Haven’t Matched Again
articles.summary: Everyone has their own interpretation about what makes a great movie villain. Some say it’s how multilayered the character is, others might debate over the scope of their evil plans, and still others would rate them based on how unique their style and/or weapon of choice is. In any case, it’s close to impossible to […]
articles.content:
Whatever criteria one might use to assess the greatest cinematic villains of all time, Hopkins’ Hannibal Lecter certainly fits the bill. Released in 1991, The Silence of the Lambs became a pop culture phenomenon, winning over both audiences and critics with its gruesome crime procedural tale based on Thomas Harris’ 1988 novel. The movie ultimately made Oscars history as the third ever (and most recent) film to win the top five categories, including Best Picture, Best Actress for Jodie Foster, and Best Actor for Hopkins himself. Yet, cinema as a whole still hasn’t managed to top what the actor achieved in The Silence of the Lambs .

Right from its release date on Valentine’s Day, The Silence of the Lambs knew exactly how to leverage its lightning-in-a-bottle charm. The film focuses on a young FBI trainee named Clarice Starling (Foster), who ends up seeking the help of the infamous Hannibal Lecter (Hopkins) to catch another serial killer, known only as Buffalo Bill (Ted Levine). More than just a crime drama, the film crossed over as one of the only horror films to become a major awards contender, thanks to its strong themes , intricate plotting, and of course, the chemistry between its two leads. Indeed, the relationship between Starling and Lecter, of course, is key to the film’s story, but what surprised everyone involved is how Hopkins made the character his own. Here’s a look at his introduction in the film:

Notably, director Michael Mann has previously adapted Harris’s Red Dragon into the 1986 film Manhunter , which featured Brian Cox in a supporting role as Lecter. Although Cox’s performance has its fans, it was Hopkins’ Lecter who became a pop cultural phenomenon. Even more remarkably, The Silence of the Lambs created an unforgettable screen villain without ever asking fans to understand him. Rather than offering an insight into his mind or some clue as to why he does the horrific things he does, director Jonathan Demme trusts Hopkins to draw in audiences without seeking their empathy. Throughout the film, Lecter demonstrates even he has a sense of etiquette despite his savage crimes. But he remains a mystery by the time the credits roll. Today, far too few mainstream villains are allowed to exist without sympathy. After all, nothing is more terrifying than the unknown.

Given the success of The Silence of the Lambs and the wealth of source material, the film was far from the last time moviegoers saw Lecter on screen. A decade later, Hopkins reprised his role opposite Julianne Moore’s Clarice Starling in Hannibal, who took the role after Foster turned it down. And its success in turn led to 2002’s Red Dragon , a prequel to The Silence of the Lambs which marked Hopkins’ third and final performance as Lecter. However, in 2016, Hopkins told The Wrap he regrets his two follow-ups to The Silence of the Lambs , calling them “mistakes” and reaffirming he wouldn’t play Lecter again.

Since Hopkins’ run, Lecter’s most iconic portrayal has been on the NBC TV series Hannibal , which ran from 2013 to 2015. On that show, Mads Mikkelsen manages to carve out his own niche as the character, wholly disparate from Hopkins’ take. And he does so by largely upholding the mystery surrounding his origin. Notably, the only film released since Red Dragon to feature Lecter was the prequel tale Hannibal Rising , which explored his origins and initial crimes. The film received poor reviews and was a box office disappointment, perhaps underscoring that some villains are best left unexplored too deeply.

Where does Anthony Hopkins’ Hannibal Lecter rank among all-time movie villains? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Turns Out, When You Play A Disney Princess They Let You Sleep In Walt's Disneyland Apartment
articles.summary: Call me Maleficent, because I'm green with envy!
articles.content:
As a Disneyland expert and superfan, there are a few items on my bucket list that I know I’ll probably never do. Those include dining at Club 33 and getting a chance to sleep inside Sleeping Beauty’s Castle. It turns out, there’s another thing that’s so exclusive I didn’t even know it was an option: sleep in Walt’s former Disneyland apartment over the newly updated Pirates of the Caribbean attraction.

First, Goodwin gets to play the original Disney Princess Snow White in the hit ABC drama Once Upon A Time , and then she gets to voice Zootopia 's Judy Hopps , one of the most beloved animated rabbits. And now, she gets to go to Disneyland whenever she wants and get to stay the night in the park. It's not like I’m totally not jealous or anything! Seriously, though, what I love is that she can appreciate the privilege, given she's a fellow Disney fanatic. Check out this recap from her late 2025 trip to Walt Disney World Resort:

Most Disneyland fans are likely aware of Walt’s apartment above the firehouse on Main Street, which guests previously were able to visit through a paid guided tour. However, many might not know that the space above the Pirates of the Caribbean attraction was also an apartment built for Walt and his family to stay and entertain guests at, since the aforementioned firehouse apartment was too small. Unfortunately, Disney passed before the suite was completed, and his brother opted to halt construction.

Unfortunately, for me and Goodwin, the apartment of Pirates of the Caribbean is no longer an option for hosting an in-park sleepover. In 2017, the space was reimagined into an exclusive dining experience, 21 Royal . Technically, this experience is open to all guests, but it comes with a pretty hefty price tag: $18,000 for up to 12 guests. I guess that’s another item I’m definitely not going to cross off my bucket list!

articles.title: Marvel Star's Unfairly Panned Superhero Movie Deserves to be Watched Before It Leaves Netflix
articles.summary: Courtesy of Summit Entertainment Comic book movies have been arriving thick and fast in the last decade, and many adaptations of these have been largely successful in capturing audiences. However, there are some that have not landed quite as expected, while others that have been panned by both critics and audiences to the point that no one wants to […]
articles.content:
Just like many movies to have been dismissed on their debut, Hellboy is one that did not necessarily do anything wrong other than arriving in the shadow of what came before it. Much of the criticism faced by the reboot directly referenced the two previous movies by Guillermo del Toro, with reviews directly comparing the different versions instead of focusing on Neil Marshall's take based on its own merits. This was always going to end unfavorably with del Toro's movies having only released in 2004 and 2008 as instant fan-favorites. While del Toro was never offered the chance to complete his trilogy, and Perlman would only return if the director was onboard , the franchise changed hands and the resulting movie was branded as an unworthy adaptation before it even released for simply not being the movie that fans had waited a decade for.

When Hellboy is viewed without the tinted lens of knowing what came before it, the film is not actually as bad as it's abysmal 17% Tomatometer score suggests. The film abandoned the whimsical tone of del Toro's movies and instead leans backwards into the R-rared horror and violence of Mike Mignola's original comics. The storyline is a loose adaptation of several arcs, resulting in a sprawling plot where Hellboy encounters Nimue the Blood Queen, an ancient resurrected sorceress looking for revenge for a previous betrayal. Stuck in the middle of a battle between the supernatural and human worlds, Hellboy realizes he must stop Nimue while trying to avoid bringing about the end of the world. For anyone who has read Mignola's stories, this was a pretty good attempt to bring them to life and certainly did not earn the hate it receive.

If there is one thing that everyone agreed on about Hellboy , it is that David Harbour certainly isn't lacking in his enthusiasm for the the role and even the harshest reviews still singled him out for throwing himself into it with both feet. Additionally, the practical effects really stood out with fearsome creature costumes and make-up bringing nightmares of page to life brilliantly . While the movie wasn't helped by reported problems behind the scenes, with Marshall disowning the movie saying he did not have the final cut on the film and stated “there's nothing of me in that movie.” Yet that should not deter you from giving Hellboy a run out before December 1, especially those who like something a little darker and gorier than in del Toro's movies. View it without expectations and you may actually have a good time in the company of this version of the half-demon.

Which version of Hellboy was your favorite? Is it Ron Perlman, David Harbour, or what about Jack Kesy in 2024's The Crooked Man ? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Johnny Depp Didn’t Just Leave Hollywood. He Left The US
articles.summary: Jack Sparrow isn't the only one who appreciates a private island.
articles.content:
Johnny Depp is officially back in Hollywood, at least as far as his career is concerned. His 2026 movie release , Ebenezer , just topped the domestic box office, marking his first major studio release in eight years. But while the actor is making his way back onto movie screens ( even for lesser pay ), he's apparently in no hurry to return to living in the United States. In fact, he's been spending most of his time somewhere that sounds an awful lot like a vacation destination.

I suppose having your own island makes avoiding the paparazzi considerably easier. And considering how much attention Depp's personal life has received over the years, I can understand why he'd want somewhere he can go about his day without somebody pointing a camera at him.

A wooden house, a yurt and somewhere to paint. Not exactly what I would have pictured for the man who spent years playing one of Disney's most recognizable characters, but I can appreciate the appeal.

His current living situation is especially interesting considering how frequently his family moved when he was growing up. Depp recalled relocating approximately 40 times during his childhood, particularly after his family moved from Kentucky to Florida. The constant changes made it difficult to settle in, and he described himself as an outsider.

Of course, his relationship with Hollywood became considerably more complicated in recent years. Depp stepped away from major American studio productions amid legal battles with his ex-wife, Amber Heard , including their highly publicized 2022 defamation trial. He continued working internationally, appearing in the French film Jeanne du Barry and directing Modi: Three Days on the Wing of Madness .

articles.title: 5 Times DC Changed a Superhero's Look and Got It Completely Wrong
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of DC Comics Superhero redesigns typically go one of two ways. Either the new costume is accepted and praised as a fresh take that captures the spirit of the character, or they are horrible looks that make you question if this is the same character at all. There are plenty of bad designs that simply aren't appealing, but […]
articles.content:
Wally West's Flash costume has always been a reflection of his journey. He started wearing a copy of Barry's, but designed his own updated version when he finally stepped out of his shadow. His 2016 Rebirth suit was beloved for combining his Kid Flash design with his Flash costume, but as sad as people were to see it go, it was hard to complain about Wally once again wearing his classic costume as he took over as the main Scarlet Speedster . However, the same can't be said for his costume for the first run in The Flash (2023), which involved big swathes of black, various specks of yellow, and a redesigned cowl.

Simply put, there's way too much going on with this design. Wally's costumes, and most iconic costumes in general, are typically simple but effective, as they are meant to be drawn in a variety of different ways, dozens of times a month. This is especially true for Wally, who is in constant motion and has a massive character investment in his costume specifically. The black bits also seem arbitrarily thrown on and break up the red in the strangest ways. The Flash has always been a character who rocked the brightest colors he could, and while this provides contrast, it doesn't really look right on Wally. Especially when he's at rest. Overall, a fine suit, but definitely not a Flash suit.

This redesign didn't just give us a new costume, but an entirely new character. Lobo's New 52 incarnation is infamous for revealing that the bastich we know and love was actually an imposter, insisting that the real Lobo was what looks to be an edgy teenager's original character. Lobo has one of the most distinctly '90s designs of all time, and that works in his favor. The original was a hulking, leather-jacket-wearing alien biker who rode a space motorcycle and used a massive spiked chain as a weapon. It's over-the-top and explosive to the point of circling back around to being cool. He works because he's a living relic who embodies all the zany, insane energy that saturated '90s comics.

The new Lobo threw all of that away, becoming a former palace guard who mourned the death of his planet and served as a bounty hunter while still maintaining that former sense of nobility, in a way. He has a much sleeker, more modern design that was meant to be cool and intimidating to a current audience. In other words, this version threw away everything that made Lobo actually work, keeping nothing fans actually went to a Lobo comic for. Worst of all, this design screams that it wants to be taken seriously, which is the last thing Lobo should ever be. It missed the entire point of why people like Lobo, and it's no mistake fans like to treat this like a painful memory from middle school.

Kyle is an artist at his core , and that means that he's never been shy about redesigning his costume. He was the first Green Lantern to massively change the uniform, adding a crab-like mask and armored forearms that felt fresh and unique at the time. His new design draws clear inspiration from that, effectively being a modernized version of it. It has all the same colors in all the same places, but the armor has been smoothed out and flattened into normal cloth. It's a much cleaner redesign and new take on his classic costume, and it's an awesome design for sure, but while it's a great look, it isn't a great look for Kyle.

Kyle has one of the most distinct styles in DC, and he's never been nervous to flaunt that, but this doesn't match that. Everything is too clean and derivative of what he's done before, to the point where it feels like someone trying to emmulate Kyle's instead of something he would make himself. The biggest show is in the mask. Kyle is famous for his unique brand of masks that would never fly with any other hero, but here he has a standard Green Lantern domino mask that's shrunk and even shows his eyes. The crab-mask is an essential part of Kyle's design, but this new one is clearly trying to be more standard, which goes against everything that makes Kyle's best designs work.

Doctor Fate's design has remained largely consistent throughout his history. Sure, there are definitely changes as his comics evolve, but beyond changing the Helm of Fate's shape from its earliest days, the vast majority of his designs only change details, not anything major about the suit itself. That is not the case for whatever the heck happened to him in the '90s. The Helm of Fate was melted down to forge a dagger and Ankh-shaped throwing stars. This came about when Kent and Inza Nelson, both of whom have been Doctor Fate before, hired Jared Stevens to retrieve the artifacts of Fate, only for them both to be rejected and killed, while Jared was imbued with magical energy and did the previously mentioned forging.

This is the single most '90s comic books thing I have ever seen. Words fail me when I try to describe this character, because it's like the people writing him had a checklist of every terrible trope from that era and made sure to get them all. Nothing about this screams Doctor Fate at all, and Jared even dropped the doctor title entirely. It was a clear attempt to draw in a new audience with dark, edgy action, but all it did was alienate every actual fan. This design was an attempt to entirely rewrite Doctor Fate's character, which is a slap in the face to everyone who actually enjoys the character, and definitely the worst type of redesign.

Tim Drake needs a new direction, that much is clear. He's been stuck in limbo for nearly two decades now, torn between his past as Robin and his need to find a new identity, unable to maintain the role while Damian exists. Brian Michael Bendis attempted to give Tim exactly the new identity he needed, but went about it in the worst way. Instead of Robin, Tim became Drake , donning a brown and yellow costume that couldn't look more generic if it tried. The biggest issue with this redesign is that it does nothing to actually give Tim what he needs while providing bland, boring alternatives.

For starters, the brown costume doesn't stand out at all. It's bland and boring to the point of being repulsive, and he even kept his Robin mask, which exacerbates the issue even more. The biggest problem, of course, is that Drake is just his name. Instead of giving him a new superheroic identity, they just chose his last name, which is the laziest way possible that doesn't actually carve him out anything new, as fans would just assume you were specifying who you mean when you say it. This wasn't even Tim's idea, as he stole it from an evil version of himself. This redesign didn't give Tim anything. If anything, it felt like it was made purposefully to call out all the problems he has while addressing none of them, leaving him in a worse spot than before.

Redesigns can be hard, but doing them right can be incredible, such as Batman's new blue costume in Batman (2025). Which recent DC redesign do you think works perfectly? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.summary: Stranger Things star Jamie Campbell Bower, who played the fan-favorite villain Vecna/Henry Creel (and Mr. Whatsit and 001, along with a few other names) in season 4 and 5 of the show, has just shared some insights into the character that will likely make some fans very happy. Most recently, Bower has appeared in yet […]
articles.content:
However, working so closely with yet another foreboding villain— Charlie Vickers' Sauron —has given Bower cause to reflect a bit more on Vecna, about one year after Stranger Things concluded for good. Specifically, speaking exclusively with ComicBook , Bower reflected on the extent to which Henry/Vecna was a tragic character, which has been a hot topic in the fanbase since it was revealed that 001, Henry, and Vecna were one in the same in season 4. While there are still heated debates on both sides of this argument, Bower shared his perspective on Vecna as a villain, and his comments are likely to please many in the fanbase who have long taken issue with how Vecna's story ended in season 5. Check out Bower's exact comments below.

Speaking about whether he sees Vecna as tragic, Bower said, “There was a tragedy to him because there was, at the core of that character, a little boy, you know, who had an experience that changed his life dramatically. So, he wasn't created as the embodiment of evil. He was created as a person. That's who he was.” The latter, in particular, was in reference to Bower's Rings of Power co-star Vickers describing Sauron as “the embodiment of evil.” Even outside of the Rings of Power connection, however, this is a significant addition to the larger conversation about Henry Creel. Specifically, with the prequel play The First Shadow , audiences learned that young Henry had been controlled by the Mind Flayer just as Will Byers had once been.

This led to considerable sympathy for the character—even the evil adult version—because it was clear that Henry had been a victim as a child. Audience expectations were therefore high that Stranger Things season 5 would, at the very least, dive deeper into this more complex aspect of Henry/Vecna's history, if not redeem him, but in the end, many felt that they wanted more empathy for him than what was shown on screen. It's therefore nice to know that, at least from Bower's perspective (who seems like the expert on the matter), there was actually something tragic to Henry, and the fact that he had this experience as a child is an essential part of his story and of understanding the character.

articles.title: At Least Robert Pattinson Looks the Part…According to Ian Fleming
articles.summary: The Bond author commissioned a sketch of 007 in the 1950s — and it bears an uncanny resemblance to a certain British actor currently being fitted for a tuxedo.
articles.content:
Well, it took nearly 70 years, and there were plenty of detours along the way, but Ian Fleming finally got the James Bond of his dreams — at least when it comes to jawline and nose shape.

None of the previous 007s — not Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan, or even Daniel Craig — looked anything like how the character's creator envisioned him. In Fleming's mind — at least according to the SMERSH dossier occasionally referred to in his books — Bond was about six-foot tall, 168 pounds, with black hair and blue eyes. For Pattison, that's check, check, check and check. But for the actors who proceeded him, not so much. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies James Bond Fans Already Complaining About Robert Pattinson: "Not Alpha Male" Movies How 'Twilight' Predicted Robert Pattinson's James Bond Casting

Connery and Lazenby had dark hair but brown eyes. Craig had blue eyes but fair hair (controversial coloring that inspired more than a few cheeky headlines when he was cast: "No Mr. Blonde, They Expect You To Dye"). Moore had blue eyes but his hair was shades too light. Brosnan came closest, with black hair and blue eyes. But it turns out Fleming had other criteria aside from basic coloring and measurements.

In fact, the author commissioned a portrait of Bond in the 1950s, years before the movies were launched, when a British newspaper purchased the rights to serialize the novels as a cartoon strip. To help the paper's illustrator nail down the look, Fleming hired an unknown artist to sketch 007's face according to his highly specific instructions ("I think we should avoid giving Bond an American-shaped head and a duck's haircut," he wrote in one note).

The result was a long angular face with heavy brows, a narrow nose, sharp cheekbones, thin lips and a firm, squared-off chin that looks uncannily like… Robert Pattinson . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The funny thing is, the newspaper's illustrator, John McLusky, pretty much ignored Fleming's ideas and drew his own Bond with a much more rugged appearance — narrower eyes, a more expansive jawline, and a broad, cleft chin. In other words, a face that looked uncannily like… Sean Connery, who'd be cast in the part a half-decade later.

articles.title: An Unorthodox Star Wars Viewing Order Has Been Proposed By a Star Wars Icon & It Actually Makes Sense
articles.summary: Darth Maul voice actor Sam Witwer has just entered the chat regarding the proper Star Wars viewing order, and although his might be the most unique suggestion thus far, it actually makes sense—especially given the audience that he has in mind. Perhaps because George Lucas began with what is technically Episode 4 (although Lucas had […]
articles.content:
Almost as popular is the approach of watching the movies in chronological order, beginning with Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace and then going from there. Over the years, though, there have been many suggestions made, from how to incorporate the TV shows to watching Episodes 4, 5, 3, and then 6, and more. Amid the many perspectives on how one should best watch Star Wars is Witwer's new suggestion, which involves beginning with Star Wars: The Clone Wars . While that might sound like blasphemy, Witwer does actually have a good point. Check out his exact comments below.

Although Star Wars fans largely resisted The Clone Wars at first, likely in large part because it only arrived three years after Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith , which was heavily criticized, it ultimately became seen as one of the franchise's best TV shows, if not the single best Star Wars TV show overall. From the introduction of Ahsoka Tano, who is now a fan-favorite character, to how much more significantly Anakin Skywalker is fleshed out as a character in the series, The Clone Wars has many merits that make in a solid addition to the galaxy far, far away. However, those aren't the reasons that Witwer believes The Clone Wars is the best place in the Star Wars timeline to start for young viewers.

Per Star Wars Holocron , Witwer said, “Here's my theory. I think you start with Clone Wars . And you don't have to start with all of it, just a lot of it. For kids, start with The Clone Wars . Get them used to what that world is and, more importantly, get them used to who Anakin Skywalker is. And then if you show them Episode IV and Obi-Wan's like, you know, Darth Vader killed your father, Anakin Skywalker, and then the kids are gunning for Darth Vader. And as long as you don't show them the prequels before that, they won't make that connection.”

Witwer continued, “So, then when you go to Episode V, you get ‘I am your father,' and then the kids are mind blown even more than you and me were mind blown, because they liked the guy, they mourned his loss, they went after the guy that killed him, to find out that's the same guy. And that's mind-blowing for them. And then once you hit Episode 5, then show them the prequels. And then at the end, which is really cool, when the droid [in Episode III] says [Padmé] is carrying twins, [the kid] is like pause, pause, pause, there is another?!” Witwer's comments are no doubt going to prove controversial, as this is certainly an unusual approach to Star Wars, and it means (in a way) usurping both the prequels and the original trilogy.

Even so, especially as an entry point for kids, The Clone Wars does make considerable sense, and Witwer actually makes great points for why, narratively, this would be an interesting approach.

articles.title: John Oliver Fills in for Tom Papa at Michael J. Fox Foundation Gala After FAA Ground Stop

articles.content:
By Saturday, air travel across the U.S. had resumed after the Federal Aviation Administration's four-hour nationwide ground stop on Friday .

But the effects of the stoppage were still unfolding, including in the entertainment world. At Saturday night's Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research gala in New York, host Denis Leary told the crowd that while they were fortunate that not many of the stars set to appear were affected by the ground stop, stand-up comedian Tom Papa, who was scheduled to perform at the benefit, was stuck in Los Angeles due to the grounding. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Grammys: Michael J. Fox, Tim Curry, 'Wicked: For Good,' 'The Pitt' Among Hollywood Nominees Lifestyle Baby2Baby Gala Fetes Demi Moore and Raises Over $20M for the Cause

In fact, he'd boarded his flight and was about to take off before the FAA ground stop on Friday.

But luckily the Michael J. Fox Foundation found another stand-up comedian in New York who could fill in: John Oliver . The Last Week Tonight host was a surprise performer at the star-studded annual benefit, where he initially joked that he was disappointing the audience after they'd already been told the scheduled comedian wasn't coming and Leary got the crowd thinking maybe Jon Stewart would be filling in since he mentioned that Oliver knows Stewart.

The FAA flight stoppage also served as fodder for fellow stand-up and Jon Stewart associate, Josh Johnson, as the Daily Show host used the beginning of his stand-up set to poke fun at Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's reality TV past on The Real World: Boston and how the way he'd said a cyberattack wasn't responsible for Friday's ground stop (the FAA insisted the pause was due to air traffic control communication issues) made Johnson think it was definitely a cyberattack. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Johnson also got some mileage out of the Microsoft outage that lasted from midday Thursday into early Friday , joking that it was great for people who were bad at their jobs, because they could simply claim they sent an email that no one could check.

“This is a dream come true for a low-tier employee,” he said.

Elsewhere at the event, which raised a record-breaking $6 million, former Late Show hosts Stephen Colbert and David Letterman made separate appearances where they jokingly stressed their ongoing relevance despite their CBS late night shows coming to an end.

Colbert joked, as he introduced a video of scientists working on medical treatments for Parkinson's as the Fox Foundation aims to find a cure for the neurodegenerative disorder, that being at the glitzy event at the Waldorf-Astoria in Manhattan made him “feel like [he has] a job.” And Letterman complimented the well-heeled audience in the hotel ballroom as he took a video on his phone to “prove to people that he's still in show business.”

The event ended with what's become a tradition at the gala of Fox joining the headlining musician onstage for a Back to the Future -inspired rendition of “Johnny B. Goode.” This year, Fox joined John Mayer and Brad Paisley along with No Doubt's Tom Dumont and Shoshana Bean. And Mayer, like Chris Martin , shared that the “new sound” Fox showed off as Marty McFly had made him want to pick up a guitar when he was a kid.

At the end of the benefit, Fox grabbed the microphone and joked that being able to perform with Mayer, Paisley and others was “definitely worth having Parkinson's for” and expressed a renewed commitment to finding a cure. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

“We're gonna get it done,” he said.

Earlier on the red carpet , Fox's friends and former colleagues spoke about how happy they were that he'd been able to return to acting this year in Shrinking .

“When I saw the footage I said, ‘This is such a perfect pairing [of Fox and Harrison Ford's character who has Parkinson's], under a perfect premise,'” Leary told The Hollywood Reporter .

Fox's former Spin City co-star Alan Ruck suggested that the work done through Fox's foundation and improvements in Parkinson's treatments may have contributed to him being able to act again.

“I know that the medicine has improved a lot since the year 2000, because that's when he stepped away from Spin ,” Ruck offered. “Because it wasn't enough for him to go to work. It was debilitating. But the medicine has improved so much, now he's on Shrinking . He's done a number of things since then so that's encouraging that all of this research is paying off. And through this foundation, he is helping people's lives improve.”

And Leary, who'd worked with Fox on FX's Rescue Me , teased that he might have another acting gig for his friend.

“I think he's a great actor. So I jealously always want to create a character for him in whatever I'm doing. So I'm actually thinking about creating a character for him in this next thing I'm going to do,” Leary told THR .

Other stars who attended the event included Christopher Lloyd, Clark Gregg, Ted McGinley, Susie Essman, Ali Wentworth, George Stephanopoulos, Willie Geist and Terry Crews, whose wife Rebecca King Crews has been living with Parkinson's, going public with her diagnosis earlier this year .

articles.title: I Didn’t Think Hallmark Could Find Another Way To Reinvent The Time Loophole Wheel, But They Crushed It
articles.summary: I was thrown for a loop!
articles.content:
Some spoilers for The Nights Before Christmas can be found in this piece.

Such core elements are so ingrained in the genre that it can be hard to reinvent the time-loop wheel, but by some miracle, Hallmark managed to do just that. And it totally worked!

Unlike other time-loop films, The Nights Before Christmas doesn’t start on day one of Marty’s loop. Instead, we meet Marty in one of the hundreds, if not thousands, of Christmas Eves he’s managed to live through. This is in immediate deviation from the genre that has made finding out you're in a time loop and freaking out about it one of the main features of a character’s arc. He’s also not freaked out or bothered by the sudden change in how time progresses; if anything, he welcomes and loves it.

The film continues to reinvent the wheel as it progresses. For starters, almost every time Marty explains to Chloe that he’s stuck in a time loop, she believes him. This is unheard of with these types of films, as most of the time the stuck character has to jump through extravagant hoops to get anyone to believe and help them. Perhaps it helps that Marty isn’t asking for Chloe’s help in getting unstuck or advice on how to survive said time loop ; he simply wants to spend time with her.

articles.title: The MCU's 5 Most Gifted Fighters Confirmed for Avengers: Doomsday, Including a Hero Unseen for Years
articles.summary: The Avengers have fought some very scary bad guys, but what makes Earth's Mightiest Heroes truly formidable is their ability to survive these incredible fights. The MCU definitely has some seriously skilled combatants on their side. Sure, having superhuman strength will definitely come in handy when Thanos shows up on your doorstep, but being able […]
articles.content:
The excitement arises from how Avengers: Doomsday assembles all kinds of fighters from across the Marvel universe. Some are professional assassins, some have spent many years battling the worst criminals on the planet, and one beloved hero finally makes his triumphant comeback. Since Marvel has announced an enormous cast, there will be a number of fearsome warriors to look forward to seeing in battle. Here are five who could provide some seriously spectacular fight scenes.

Channing Tatum is returning to his role as Remy LeBeau in Avengers: Doomsday and this is a controversial move for X-Men fans. Personally, I wanted to see a leaner actor with sharp features and a natural Cajun accent. But the character was first introduced in a very successful Deadpool & Wolverine . Regardless, there's more to him than throwing explosive cards in his enemies' faces. Remy LeBeau is also a highly skilled combatant and he doesn't just defeat his enemies with his energy abilities. Instead, the guy's a really exceptional gymnast and incorporates a lot of serious martial arts with his fighting. In the comics, he's known for his acrobatics and gymnastics. His staff is obviously his weapon of choice, and he's learned to use it best from the art of Bojutsu. He also has deep French roots which is why he's also a fan of Savate, or French Kickboxing.

Naturally, Gambit's mutant powers make him even more lethal. He's able to imbue objects with kinetic energy, and practically anything he touches can become a deadly weapon. His signature playing cards are always fun, but it's easy to imagine the kind of chaos he'd sow with an arsenal to go along with that attitude. He's also a talented thief and has plenty of practice getting himself out of a jam. This time around, he'll get to embrace it in a bigger Marvel franchise.

Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler is another pretty excellent addition to Avengers: Doomsday . We haven't seen him in a significant live-action X-Men film since 2003's X2 , which is kind of a long time for a guy who was introduced so memorably. This also finally gives Marvel the chance to put one of the more visually spectacular fighters of the X-Men universe into the MCU. If you think he's strange to look at, you've made a big mistake.

It's his teleportation powers that make him nearly unbeatable in a fight. It's not hard to imagine him vanishing in a puff of smoke and suddenly popping up completely out of range from whatever enemy he's facing. That's a leg up on the competition right there. He's also an acrobatic and dangerous fighter and has plenty of experience working alongside the X-Men, especially in that eye-popping opening scene in X2 where he teleports across the entire length of a building and takes out people. But in the comics, he's even a better fighter. He's got more of a swashbuckler style due to his upbringing in a Bavarian circus. He idolized the very real actor Errol Flynn and his exceptional swordplay. It was in the Excalibur comics where he truly mastered the title of swordsman with cutlasses, fencing sabers, and rapiers. And before Zoro from One Piece , Nightcrawler already had a third sword held in his tail for a 3-sword fighting style!

Fans seem to have accepted Florence Pugh's Yelena Belova, and it is easy to see why she is one of the most interesting characters in the MCU so far. She's also a badass fighter. Yelena was born in the Red Room, where she was trained from a young age to be a professional assassin like Natasha Romanoff. For this reason, she is comfortable using just about any weapon or fighting style in close quarters.

Yelena is interesting because she doesn't require super powers to be on par with some of the most dangerous characters in the Marvel universe. Her combat training, reflexes, and fighting instincts make her a force to reckon with and not afraid to get down and dirty with a stronger opponent. Not the worst quality to have when facing off against a villain like Doctor Doom. Black Widow , Hawkeye , and Thunderbolts have proven Yelena can be one of the most formidable human fighters in the MCU. Her next opponent may be the biggest challenge of all.

Sebastian Stan's Bucky Barnes was at Steve Rogers' side before HYDRA turned him into the Winter Soldier. Years of being brainwashed made Bucky an extremely lethal assassin who could match even the most powerful foes in the world. His metal arm helps, but his prowess in combat has more than a little to do with his abilities.

Bucky is also trained in decades of military combat, and is armed with guns and knives. He's no stranger to taking on super soldiers and professional killers, having gone head to head with Captain America and Black Panther. And he's come a long way since he last served as a HYDRA assassin, having grown into his own man. Which is why his return is so interesting: Bucky isn't going to be fighting as a hero following orders – he's going to be fighting for his own sake. And he's got plenty of experience in the bank, and if Doctor Doom underestimates him, he could be in for a shock.

It's been a while since we last saw this Kung-fu master. We first met Simu Liu as the martial-arts hero in his eponymous film, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings , but he disappeared without much ado after the movie's release in 2021. Now, almost two years since the blockbuster premiered, the actor is coming back to us, and to an even bigger screen in Avengers: Doomsday . Hopefully, the wait will be worth it.

Shang-Chi isn't just another superhero with a handful of fight moves in their back pocket. He's one of the best martial artists in the entire MCU, and since his father trained him to be a fighter from a young age, he's turned his skills into a real force of nature. Not to mention, Shang-Chi's got the Ten Rings. With those on his side, he's got an incredible advantage, not to mention the ability to combine mystic energy projection attacks with martial arts fighting. He's already proven he can hold his own with some dangerous enemies, so getting him into an Avengers movie seems like a no-brainer.

Which of these Avengers fighters are you most excited to see in action in Avengers: Doomsday? Do you think anyone else deserves a spot on this list? Share your thoughts and let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: Rob Riggle Saw 'Nickels' As a Way to Branch Out from Comedy
articles.summary: Riggle and director Spencer King discuss the drama, about a man who comes to believe a neighbor may be the reincarnated spirit of his late brother.
articles.content:
For Rob Riggle , Nickels was a chance to show off another color in his performing palette. The actor is known for his comedy chops, with scene stealing work in the Jump Street movies and Step Brothers , but in the new film, he plays a man who has long grieved the death of his brother in a motorcycle crash decades earlier. After a college-aged neighbor Mitch (Aaron Holliday) has his own motorcycle accident, Riggle's character, Tom Monroe, starts to wonder if this young man has become a reincarnation of his brother. There are similiarities too eery to miss, though the audience could interpret it a number of ways, including perhaps the neighbor is misleaidng Tom. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies 'Jimmy' Review: KJ Apa Tries, in Vain, to Save Ploddingly Dutiful James Stewart Biopic Movies 'The Wilderness' Filmmaker Spencer King Signs with Rewind Artists (Exclusive)

The film took shape thanks to another Tom — Briarcliff boss Tom Ordenberg, who got ahold of the script from Tim Tuchrello and approached director Spencer King , who'd grown up with Ordenberg's son. From there, Ordenberg suggested Riggle for the lead, and the actor signed on after a Zoom with King, who beamed in from a truck stop in Utah, where he was working on his previous movie, The Wilderness .

Over a quick 19 days, King and Riggle filmed the movie around Los Angeles, with Odessa A'zion playing Riggle's onscreen daughter and Elizabeth Tulloch also starring as his wife. After a theatrical release last month, the film is available on PVOD via Briarcliff.

Rob, you've been on a lot of sets. Was there anything unusual about this experience?

ROB RIGGLE When you shoot a film that's on a tight on schedule, there's just no time to screw around. You've got to focus. And that's why having a director that has a vision and knows what he or she wants to grab is a must-have before you can move to the next setup. Spencer brings that level of confidence to the set. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

SPENCER KING It's also why you need a lead actor who is an ex-Marine. Keep everyone in line. ( Laughs. )

As a guy with a beard, I appreciated yours here, Rob. Whose choice was that?

RIGGLE I think it was my girlfriend's idea. And then I got it approved by Spencer. That also just cuts down on makeup time a lot.

There's a potential supernatural element here. Spencer, did you have a dial in your head of how far you wanted to take it?

KING For me, it's a film where you can kind of bring your own faith into it. You can bring your own perspectives on the world and your own spirituality. The film isn't trying to convince you of thinking any differently. For me, the interesting tidbit was not, is he the brother or is he not? It's, does he believe he's the brother? Or does Mitch believe he's Tom's brother? Or is he messing him?

Rob, you got to shoot this at home in L.A. How often have you shot in L.A. over the last decade?

RIGGLE It probably has been over a decade. I've shot some television here, but as far as a feature film, it might have been the Catalina wine mixer [from 2008's Step Brothers ]. It'd been awhile. You can't put a price tag on being able to go sleep in your own bed every night. It's a really special deal. So I consider myself incredibly lucky that we got to do that here.

Anytime you make a movie on this scale, you've got to call in favors. What were some of those you called in to make this owrk ? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

KING Equipment-wise, we called in every favor. Luke Dyra, our DP, called in all the favors and we pulled a lot of post favors.

RIGGLE Producers were also doing a lot of outreach. They were working the phones all the time. They were like, “All right, we got this location. All right, we got this motorcycle. Oh, we got this spot." They were cooking with gas the whole time.

KING For me, this was, this is one of my favorite types of movies. It's something Rob and I talked about in the production of it. A lot of my favorite movies are when more comedic actors go serious. Eternal Sunshine is one of my favorite movies. Adam Sandler's done it a handful of times, Will Ferrell and Stranger Than Fiction , and I really thought this was one of those. This has a chance to be that for Rob in a lot of ways. Not that Rob hasn't done it, but it's such a different look. I think that sometimes comedians are building up to a punchline. So there's a natural sequence for working up to a crescendo of sorts. What I felt on set and in the edit was Rob naturally was able to pinpoint the inflection point of the scene and in some sort of subtle way be able to deliver that scene's "punchline."

RIGGLE Well, you're very kind to say that. I think comedic actors, myself included, the reason we get to keep doing comedies is because hopefully we do them well. But it's like a palette of colors. I've got a lot of colors on the palette. Everybody's seen red. I can do that, but I got other colors. I can do green, I can do yellow, I can do blue, whatever you want. I think a lot of actors, especially comedy actors, don't get the opportunities. So that's another reason I was so grateful to be part of this.

articles.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Gives Players The Local Play Feature They've Wanted Most
articles.summary: Courtesy of Fuse Games A new free update is coming to Star Wars: Galactic Racer in 2027, with developer Fuse Games listening to fan feedback and adding split-screen local multiplayer to the exciting racing title. Galactic Racer has been reviewed positively since its launch in early October 2026, with players praising the game's absurdly fast speed and chaotic sci-fi […]
articles.content:
Local split-screen games have been few and far between in modern releases, even if they have a thriving online multiplayer scene like those in popular genres. That being said, racing games have long benefited from local play, as titles like Mario Kart are infamous for being a great party experience with you and several friends competing together to beat each other in fast-paced circuits. Split-screen has been a feature Star Wars: Galactic Racer fans have long wanted, and with a social media post by developer Fuse Games, it seems like players are finally getting their wish.

According to a message on Bluesky, Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a “Free Play” mode for Star Wars: Galactic Racer , a local multiplayer setting where no restrictions can plague the title. This local mode allows players to choose their vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone with AI-controlled opponents or with up to three players. Like fans have been begging for, those four players can participate in races together, putting different displays in each corner of the screen for maximum chaos in already blindingly fast competitions.

An early look from a pre-release build of Free Play mode accompanied the Galactic Racer post, showing players how UI/UX elements of the game will be organized in split-screen. Thankfully, players will also be able to use Free Play to queue up two player or three player matches, with the screen likely dividing in different ways to accommodate everyone involved. At the bare minimum, the mode can be used to practice on various planets and tracks, getting players used to certain environmental conditions of specific worlds that are giving them trouble in the main story.

Similarly, this mode can be used to memorize tracks, getting players familiar with every shortcut, twist, and turn they can expect during a race. Much like its inspirations of F-Zero and Burnout , Star Wars: Galactic Racer is adapting to players who desperately want to master the game after completing its roguelike story mode. Online multiplayer will still be around, of course, but local play vastly expands the replay potential of Galactic Racer for years to come.

The four-player split screen increases the longevity of Star Wars: Galactic Racer , which may push Fuse Games to expand upon the features already in the title. Alongside Star Wars Zero Company , Galactic Racer is an extremely impressive Star Wars project, both due to its deep racing mechanics and unapologetic difficulty at times that players have to overcome. There are many layers to Galactic Racer ‘s design , from small modifiers contributing to a big impact during races to the unique qualities of each in-game planet that change how you need to approach various tracks. To that point, the game has the building blocks to grow over time with an expansion or DLC content.

Local multiplayer might put Galactic Racer over the top to get the support it needs for DLC, either in the form of new vehicles to entirely new maps. Having an extra planet with multiple race tracks would be a dream come true, although new story circuits wouldn't be bad either. One of the biggest complaints for Galactic Racer right now is that it is light on content, so split-screen is a huge boost for getting other content green lit. Hopefully, 2027's update is just the start of things to come, with talk about Star Wars: Galactic Racer for multiple awards setting up continued support even more.

How will you be enjoying the four player split-screen update for Star Wars: Galactic Racer ? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.title: PC Game With 100% User Review Score Now Free on Steam

articles.content:
Naturally, it's not the biggest game, and it's working with a humble budget, but the new Steam game Helena: Cloud District has impressed Steam users. We know this because after 149 user reviews, it has a 100% approval rating. There is not a single negative review, only positive. Of course, the game being given away for free earns it favor, but it also lowers the barrier to entry, which works against its review score as well. To this end, most free Steam games do not have a 100% user review score. Some get close, but it's rare for a game not to have a single negative review across an appreciable number of reviews.

As for the game itself, for those just learning about it, Helena: Cloud District is an atmospheric first-person exploration platformer game where you freely explore a decaying mega structure of mysterious origin “to photograph strange plants and uncover fragments of melancholic memories.” The game is not very long, only taking about one to two hours to beat, but despite being short, it's left an impression on those who have played it.

Steam Users Are Enjoying It “Moveset and game-feel are just so good; this is a really great idea,” reads the most popular user review for the game on Steam. “I love the level art and the level design too, really impressed by this work.”

Another user review adds, “Really interesting game. Only about an hour long, but it kept me interested the whole time. Love the design of the world.”

As you would expect, this is the highest-rated free Steam game release in a while. Why the game is free and what future plans for it are, we do not know. In terms of free Steam games, though, it is one of the better ones of 2026, and one of the more unique ones as well.

If this new free Steam game doesn't tickle your fancy, there are other options, including a new horror game earning similarly glowing user reviews . Meanwhile, for those with a little money to spend, a 2000s GameCube game just came to Steam with a new remaster , and it's shot toward the top of the Steam charts.

Josh Hutcherson has also expressed warm feelings about the reception he’s received for his performance as Peeta, which has blown fans away . Over the last few years, leading documentary festival IDFA has become a crucial stop on the awards season trail, with major streamers and key studios courting voters in Amsterdam's imposing 17th-century canalside houses and theaters. One of the key titles in this year's best documentary race, however, has foregone glitzy cocktails and receptions in favor of a lengthy on-stage conversation, with the team behind " NAZA " filling the DeLaMar theater on a rainy Monday night to discuss how the film "broke the mold" in terms of finding audiences. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Toni Collette to Lead Apple TV Dramedy 'Lenni' Based on Norwegian Format São Paulo Grand Prix 2026: Here's Where to Watch F1 Online for Free

The panel saw a rare public appearance by director Yuval Abraham, who connected via Zoom from London, where he continues to tackle his journalism work for "NAZA" producer The Guardian , represented on the IDFA stage by editorial director, film and TV and head of documentaries Lindsay Poulton. Abraham and Poulton were joined by the film's producer James Wilson ("The Zone of Interest") and Fionnuala Jamison, managing director of major sales agent MK2. Rachel Szor, who directed the film alongside Abraham, was not present.

Asked about how it feels to tackle the overwhelming calendar of a high-profile awards campaign for a film as sensitive and somber as "NAZA," Abraham said the thought is not at the forefront of his mind. "We have so much to do with the film and also with the journalism. We're working on the investigative journalism, and I really want to focus on that."

Abraham has very recent experience with the frenzy of the awards race, having won the best documentary Oscar two years ago for "No Other Land," co-directed with Szor and Palestinian directors and activists Basel Adra and Hamdan Ballal. "The awards are important in a sense because they do give more visibility, and of course, that's what we want," he said. "But on the other hand, my experience with ‘No Other Land' has been that voters are also smart. They know the film is out there and they can watch it and make up their own mind." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"I prefer to focus on doing conversations with audiences when we feel it's meaningful," added the director. "We're planning to be physically present to meet audiences. We hope to screen the film in front of politicians all over the world, to leverage this streaming moment when it comes out on The Guardian, when Israelis and Palestinians are able to watch it online and access it, to get people to write about it and talk about it. For me, that's the focus."

Wilson echoed that thought, noting how Yuval and Szor could not be physically present in Amsterdam for the talk—or to meet with voters in the Amsterdam awards stop—because "the journalism is ongoing and they are deep in that. The killing is ongoing."

The veteran producer, who has a career spanning over three decades, noted how he has only recently been involved in films that have received awards attention: Jonathan Glazer's Oscar-winning "The Zone of Interest" and Kaouther Ben Hania's Oscar-nominated "The Voice of Hind Rajab."

"For me, it's a very simple contract in a way," he said, adding that "awards are a form of a light being shone on your film. It's a form of marketing." The producer then noted that awards also bring to attention films in "an era and an age where there is so much competition for attention and cinema is no longer the kind of jewel at the top of the cake, the summit of moving pictures."

When prodded about the lesson behind the success of "NAZA"—which has topped 1.5 million admissions worldwide and reached a $14 million box office so far—Wilson said it is "a clarion call to distributors to not be afraid of the subject matter and to open doors to it. Because when the doors are open, people come into the cinemas to see it. People who are trying to stymie that, like the people who didn't want to release ‘No Other Land,' should be ignored."

The producer was referring to how "No Other Land" struggled to get distribution in the U.S., with the filmmaking team eventually self-distributing. That experience, Abraham noted, taught him and Szor "how long it can take for a film to be accessible to wide audiences," something they thought about at length when discussing the release strategy for their follow-up. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"NAZA" was a complete mystery until it was announced as a late addition to the Venice Film Festival competition on Aug. 24. Mere days later, it played to massive acclaim at the festival, landing a record-breaking 25-minute standing ovation and winning the Special Jury Prize. During the talk, Jamison revealed the filmmakers originally intended for the film to be made available online on The Guardian the day after the festival premiere, a strategy they eventually changed after lengthy conversations with Wilson and the MK2 team.

While the film is still scheduled to be made available online for free at The Guardian sometime in December, MK2 has secured deals for theatrical exhibition in 56 territories. In the U.S., Neon acquired it following an initial rollout by the British news company and the French sales agent.

"Our north star with ‘NAZA' has always been about impact. It's how you reach people, move people, and get them talking and to be in dialogue with really important matters that are at the core of this subject. Sitting in a cinema has been an important part of that," added Poulton of the strategy, with Abraham adding that he learned from his team that "the film being immediately accessible doesn't necessarily translate to maximum impact."

Releasing "NAZA" has been a particularly challenging process given the secrecy and sensitivity surrounding the project. Because the filmmakers could "only approach people [they] trusted," that narrowed financing avenues and possible creative partners. But Wilson is quick to add that the team's decision not to show the film to industry peers before Venice was strictly tied to security. "There was no sort of sleight-of-hand mystery to the late announcement, and I've heard chatter about that."

As for the real-life impact of the film, Abraham spoke about the "violent" reaction to the film in his home country of Israel, which did not come as a shock. One of the hardest parts, however, was dealing with the effect it had on the directors' families. "Rachel's parents had these right-wing protests or mobs outside her house."

When asked if "NAZA" had changed the way the world is dealing with the ongoing “genocide” in Gaza, Wilson said he sees cinema as "an antidote to fear and the antidote to complicity in the crime," but that he could "make no claims" for the film singlehandedly being responsible for any responses to the conflict, but that the film spoke to people's moral and ethical compasses. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"It's sort of interesting to look at the midterm elections in the U.S. and these swathes of candidates being successful who have come out against the mass killing, the ethnic cleansing, the genocide, but also on other issues and [mobilizing] against other forms of authoritarian hegemony, mergers, and things like that," he said. "I like to think ‘NAZA' is a small cog in a machine of resistance."

articles.title: ‘I Know This Sounds Dark.’ The Advice Kelly Clarkson Gives Contestants When The Voice Goes Live

articles.content:
Kelly Clarkson never fails to entertain or make me emotional on The Voice . I enjoy seeing her bring out the heartfelt words of encouragement, maybe even more than I enjoy watching her attempt to steal country singers from Riley Green. (But only slightly.) She never shies away from tearing up, or channeling what she learned from her American Idol days, which is what she used to give advice to contestants whenever The Voice goes live.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Super Needs to Bring Back Frieza's Full Family
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Toei Animation Frieza has been the lone constant villain since Dragon Ball Z, and with the evil emperor still alive in the timeline, it's time to bring his entire family into the fight. Some villains might boast more strength than him, but Frieza is the most dynamic, proving that he can build upon his powers while maintaining […]
articles.content:
The only logical next step for him would be to try and destroy his longtime nemesis Goku. In order to do that, he'll need a lot of help considering the Frieza Force troop's losses over the years. The best way to counter that is to get more high-tier fighters, which is where his family comes into play. King Cold is already a part of the current canon, but probably needs some significant power boosting after his decimation at the hands of Future Trunks. Next, it's time to introduce Cooler to the Dragon Ball canon and really up the ante.

Frieza's older brother is like the non-Saiyan version of the original Broly. First introduced 35 years ago in the Dragon Ball Z film Cooler's Revenge , he's in a lot of content, but all of it is now non-canon. Unlike his brother's final form, Cooler's masked face and towering physique make him a much more imposing fighter. Cooler recently achieved the Golden Cooler form in Super Dragon Ball Heroes , so the concept is out there that he can compete with this new godly level of Saiyan power in the later releases.

Cooler provides an immediate power up to his brother's forces. However, he's not the only member of the family that can fight. King Cold, their father, built an empire on conquering worlds and destroying civilizations. His minimal appearances don't show off his skills, and his quick defeat in the lone battle he fought in undersells his skills. He's currently dead but probably got plenty of training in the afterlife, as he's currently in hell for his many vile acts. If Frieza brings him back, that family trio would definitely give the Z Fighters some problems.

The most recent on-screen appearance for Frieza came in Dragon Ball Super: Broly , but he's not sat idly by since taking a beating from the Legendary Super Saiyan. The Dragon Ball Super manga displays an even more powerful version of the villain. Frieza unveils that he found a hyperbolic time chamber that allowed him to further expand his powers and become Black Frieza in the Granolah the Survivor Saga . He defeats Goku and Vegeta easily and moves on.

His powered-up form combined with Golden Cooler, and just for fun, a transformed King Cold would provide maybe the toughest trio for Goku, Vegeta and friends to battle. Frieza is the only bad guy with the same tenacity as the Saiyan heroes and that's why even though he continually loses, his threat always looms large. The setup is there for him and his family to get a shot at revenge. Do you think they should get another shot at the Saiyans? Would you want to see the Frieza family return? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: John Patrick Shanley On His New Off Broadway Play 'Mountain Girl', Industry Upheaval And Why He "Deeply Opposed" WGA Strikes
articles.summary: John Patrick Shanley is a connoisseur of contradiction. When the New York Public Library’s main branch on Fifth Avenue comes up in conversation, the Bronx native takes note of the role of the robber barons in creating the library and other foundational parts of the city. Attending a recent wedding at the library, he says, […]
articles.content:
John Patrick Shanley is a connoisseur of contradiction. When the New York Public Library's main branch on Fifth Avenue comes up in conversation, the Bronx native takes note of the role of the robber barons in creating the library and other foundational parts of the city. Attending a recent wedding at the library, he says, "was like being in the ballroom of the Titanic. … It's the craziest opulence I have ever experienced." Citing the contribution of Andrew Carnegie to the library and other landmarks, he muses, "All those awful people did wonderful things."

The latest play from the Oscar ( Moonstruck ) and Pulitzer ( Doubt ) winner is the Off Broadway world premiere Mountain Girl , which channels his knack for extracting drama and wry comedy from life's paradoxes. The NylonFusion Theatre Company and Axial Theatre production recently opened at 154 Theatre and its run has just been extended to November 28. The show centers on Connie, an aspiring writer navigating a turbulent marriage, a highly complicated relationship with her mother, and a would-be artistic rivalry between the spouses. The play shares its title with the novel that Connie has never finished, and the show is a meditation of the craft and emotional torment of writing, or even the idea of writing. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News 'Slam Frank' Hip-Hop Musical Retelling Of Anne Frank Story Extends Off Broadway Run News Eight 'Real Housewives' To Make Off Broadway Debuts In Neil Simon's 'Rumors' Revival

Speaking with Deadline New York Business Editor Dade Hayes, Shanley detailed the play's development, which had work-in-progress presentations in L.A. in 2022 and then a five-day workshop in Paris in 2025. He also sized up the many changes in Hollywood of late, including what he considers to be self-inflicted wounds by the Writers Guild of America from its two most recent strikes.
