This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity and length.

DEADLINE: Without giving too much away, this play has potency in part because it ends up being about the messiness of something incomplete, a goal unrealized. When did that idea come to you?

JOHN PATRICK SHANLEY: I was initially interested in two writers – one can't start and one can't finish. So, one of them keeps writing and the other one can't get started. That is something that I'd experienced many years ago. And it creates its own peculiar madness. It struck me then that we do a lot of modeling in life, and that's definitely something that I'm dealing with in the play. People do things to demonstrate to their partner, ‘This is how you do that. This is how you should be acting.' The person modeling the behavior is trying to get the other person through manipulation, which is not a dirty word to me. To talk about change instead of just going ahead and changing, and that sets in motion a lot of crazy things. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

DEADLINE: You put the novel manuscript on the table, almost like Chekhov's loaded gun, right at the beginning. We expect someone to finish the book, steal credit for it, or do some conventional thing. But you're more interested in the characters' interior lives than a story of artistic inspiration.

SHANLEY: Most writers have a lot of bad writing to do. Sometimes when I talk to writers who are just starting, I'm like, ‘You have a lot of bad writing to do, you might as well get started.' It's like a road you have to go down in order to get to the destination you want. You have to go through a lot of dreary territory. But I see nobility in anyone's struggle to create something, express something. It is almost immaterial to me whether the product is good. Is the struggle noble? Is the struggle worthy? In the play, the girl, she's trying to write to please her mother. She had some talent, but then her mother got very excited because it would make the mother look good. And she immediately started to breathe down her neck, like ‘When are you going to write the next part?' and all that, and the girl got completely frozen. A kind of paralysis descended on her. So, it's sort of a Mexican standoff.

DEADLINE: I understand there's going to be a French-language production of Mountain Girl and a West End revival of your play Four Dogs and a Bone in London. What's it been like over your career to work in Europe, the UK and back home?

SHANLEY: At one point, many years ago, I did Moonstruck and I had been doing plays for a goodly while, and I ended up in Spain doing a week-long gig with [1983 play] Danny and the Deep Blue Sea working with local artists and stuff like that. They had me speak to the press. And the press's attitude towards the arts there was utterly different. The American thing was, ‘What's Cher like?!' How much did the movie cost to make?' Stuff like that. Over there, they were like, ‘You seem like you have a troubled soul. That reminds me of certain moments of Dante.' I'm sort of trying to talk the language that I learned from the journalists in America and very quickly realizing, ‘Oh, this is another whole thing, and this is more interesting to me.' I found myself doing a press junket for [1995 film] Congo , of all things. An interviewer said to me, with incredible solemnity, ‘What's it like, adapting Michael Crichton?' I looked at him and said, ‘Well, we're not talking about Thomas Hardy.' And the guy looked completely shocked.

DEADLINE: You have always managed to balance film and theater. Is that intentional?

SHANLEY: I've been fortunate. But in my head, I have visual skills as well as language skills. So I can picture things, which helps.

DEADLINE: It's been quite a daunting period of years for Hollywood, with the Skydance merger, layoffs, labor unrest, AI, Covid, on and on. Anxiety has always been common in the industry but we seem to be in uncharted waters. Are you discouraged at all by the state of things?

SHANLEY: I think that the culture is now going at a speed that none of us can keep up with. There's a constant feeling of being ungrounded. Whenever you start to get a point of view developed about what's going on with AI or what's going on with conglomerates, it changes. That's one of the reasons that theater has been so important for me. Theater will weather all this shit. It may be, you know, back to the caveman situation, but you can always get some people and even if there's no electricity go out in natural light and perform a play. The money, the technology of filmmaking can very quickly make it out of reach. There are so many very gifted writers and directors that one, and they start to do well and they move to Los Angeles and then, you know, they have like five or 10 or 15 great years. But then, if they physically survive, they usually have a really significant period where they can't work. They've completely invested in things that require large amounts of money and technology. And they've left behind the bedrock that they can depend on, and to ground themselves as individual human beings and have a relationship with the sun coming up in the morning and the moon coming up in the evening, in favor of this artificial environment. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

DEADLINE: We have written recently about New York overtaking L.A. in terms of production spending, which seemed unthinkable during the worst of Covid.

SHANLEY: I've been very concerned, especially for Los Angeles. They have been through every kind of calamity. And it's a culture utterly different than New York. New York is not a one-industry town. L.A. really is a one-industry town, and the problem is that the industry, we've gotten to be in great trouble and also great upheaval and at the same time environmentally. You know, they don't have any water. They have these enormous fires. It's this wonderful giant talent pool that had to endure multiple strikes, including the Writer's Guild strikes. I was deeply opposed to [the strikes], but I did not speak to the media about it because I felt that that would be undercutting. These guys, rightly or wrongly, they're trying to do something. I thought they were fighting battles that had already been lost and putting people on ice for significant periods of time. [Combined with Covid], it ended up being like a 5-year hiatus from work, and it's very hard to restart your career after a blow like that.

DEADLINE: Do you still go back and forth to L.A. for meetings?

SHANLEY: Very rarely. Everything that I've done pretty much has been through personal associations. When I did the [2008] film of Doubt , [producer Scott Rudin] just said, ‘Do you want to direct it?' And I said, ‘Yeah.' He said, ‘I think it's a great idea.' So I, you know, I've been lucky. [Executive producer] Steven Spielberg said that about [1990 film] Joe Versus the Volcano : ‘I hear you want to direct it.' And the truth was, I didn't remember ever saying that. But I was like, ‘Yeah, yeah.'

DEADLINE: Since you mention Joe , I wonder what it's like to have a film be so misunderstood initially by critics and the public and then go on to develop a following. People were conditioned to expect something else from a major-studio movie starring Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan.

SHANLEY: It was epic. It was almost an 80-day shoot. I was living in a hotel in Los Angeles. My assistant had a car and I got around that way. Once we started shooting, I was in fairly constant struggles with Warner Brothers because I was shooting exactly the movie I told them I would shoot. And they seemed astonished by that. And I had sort of his storyboarded the whole thing, so I'm like, ‘Why would they be surprised? It's exactly what I said.' And then, uh, you know, we did it and uh, uh, New York press in particular was savage towards it.

DEADLINE: Warner Brothers has had its share over the years – just last month with Digger . And it wasn't Warner, but look at the reversal on Ken Russell's The Devils 55 years later!

SHANLEY: Absolutely. So anyway, I crashed and burned emotionally when I got such a rough reception to Joe . I had to refine my balance, refine the way I did what I did. And I got my confidence back and my certainty of voice back. I did the screenplay for Alive , and that was solid and good, but it took time.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Boss Reveals If More Star Trek Sets Are on the Way
articles.summary: One of the lead designers in charge of Magic: The Gathering has revealed whether or not any future sets tied to Star Trek will be releasing in the future. As the latest set in MTG's Universes Beyond line, Star Trek has represented a sizable shift from Wizards of the Coast's most recent collaborations in the […]
articles.content:
Speaking on his official Tumblr page, Magic: The Gathering designer Mark Rosewater said plainly that there are “no current plans for future Star Trek sets.” Rosewater didn't get into the specifics of why this is the case, but this is the first such confirmation from someone at Wizards of the Coast about what its plans might be with Star Trek looking ahead.

Generally speaking, it's not a shock to hear that Wizards of the Coast won't do anything else with Star Trek in MTG , at least for the time being. This month's Star Trek set has received a rather mixed response since its launch, with some MTG players criticizing the artwork and new mechanics that have been seen with the latest cards. This reception led to widespread reports of pre-release events for the Star Trek set having a lower turnout when compared to past MTG releases in 2026.

Star Trek is inherently a series that is aimed more at older audiences as well, as arguably the two most popular releases in the franchise ( Star Trek: TOS and Star Trek: The Next Generation ) are quite dated. While there are surely many younger fans of the IP, it's easy to argue that it's a more niche property, especially when compared to something like Marvel or The Lord of the Rings.

Looking ahead, the next major set for Magic: The Gathering that will be released is Nauctis . Set to launch in February, this new line of cards will boast an underwater theme and will feature new creatures and artifacts related to the ocean. Nauctis will then be following by Darkhold Destiny in April, which will be MTG's third set related to Marvel. This time around, though, Darkhold Destiny will put a much larger emphasis on the mystical parts of Marvel, with characters like Dr. Strange, Scarlet Witch, Ghost Rider, and Blade being thrust into the spotlight more prominently.

How do you feel about MTG potentially only ever getting one run of Star Trek cards? And what do you think about this Star Trek set that has been released so far? Be sure to let me know for yourself in the comments below.

articles.title: Robert Pattinson As James Bond? Baz Bamigboye Has Some Thoughts
articles.summary: A wise movie-world person of my acquaintance who has resided in these British isles long enough to understand the customs of the country shook their head when they heard that Robert Pattinson had been officially cast to play Ian Fleming’s James Bond in the 007 reboot that Denis Villeneuve is in pre-production to direct. They […]
articles.content:
A wise movie-world person of my acquaintance who has resided in these British isles long enough to understand the customs of the country shook their head when they heard that Robert Pattinson had been officially cast to play Ian Fleming's James Bond in the 007 reboot that Denis Villeneuve is in pre-production to direct.

They intoned: "Bond is mysterious. Bond creates the stars. The stars don't create Bond," then added for good measure, "For f*ck's sake!"

While I don't think it's the right thing for reinventing Bond, my sense is that Pattinson will be good, though I don't think it's hardly fresh to cast a 40-year-old movie star. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

The Twilight movies catapulted Pattinson to superstardom, then he spent years shunning the limelight they brought him, becoming for a while David Cronenberg's darling in Cosmopolis and Map of the Stars .

Then he shot Robert Eggers' sublime The Lighthouse in 2019 opposite Willem Dafoe, and that was the moment I saw him in, forgive me, a different light, and began taking him seriously as an actor.

Christopher Nolan took him under his wing for Tenet and this year's The Odyssey — which he stole, along with Samantha Morton and John Leguizamo. Those three provided the heat in that epic. I made myself sick popping popcorn (so bad for my delicate teeth) when they weren't on the ginormous Imax screen.

Pattinson was at an FYC screening of Primetime on Sunday night, but he scooted away like a bat out of …you know, because he had an early call for The Batman: Part II . He's great as the Caped Crusader, but I feel Batman baggage will color how we see him as Bond.

Fleming described his creation as a "blunt instrument," and I just can't see how that will come across here. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Robert Wade and Neil Purvis, who wrote for several Bond pictures under the reign of Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, took a different tack. When I spoke to them Monday night in London they told Deadline that they reckon R Patz — as Pattinson fans call him — is "a terrific choice, very exciting."

They suggested, correctly in my ever-so-humble view, that the classically trained Daniel Craig, last of 007's parish, "is a hard act to follow in terms of chops."

They added: "But Robert has what it takes to — we liked the sly wit he brought to the spy in Tenet , and with this decision it's clear Denis wants to keep Bond cool."

See, while I agree with much of what they said, I'm kinda shaken but not at all stirred by Pattinson's casting.

Perhaps it was misdirection, and probably partly because I wanted it to be true, but I brought into this notion that Bond 26 would be cast with a relative unknown. Remember that Craig was not a big name when Broccoli and Wilson chose him for Bond. Sure, he was well admired and well known to London theatregoers, and we all marveled at his performances in the likes of Our Friends in the North when it hit BBC screens in 1996 and movies such as The Mother, Sylvia, Munich and Layer Cake . But I'd argue that he wasn't then a bona fide star; rather, he was on the cusp of becoming one.

Let's not forget that director Martin Campbell loathed the idea of casting him as Bond in Casino Royale . He and others had hated Craig's Bond screen-test.

Campbell wanted to go in a different direction, but word started filtering out from the set of Matthew Vaughn's Layer Cake that, hey, Craig's holding this movie up. A rough cut was screened for them, and Broccoli's eyes lit up. By the way, she'd always admired his stage work, and with Campbell's agreement, a second screen test was arranged — and, well, we know the rest.

I checked in with Vaughn, The Kingsman filmmaker, and he just laughed over the phone.

"When I last checked Bond is dead. Long live The Kingsman ," he said before politely putting the phone down on me.

Cheeky sod, that Matthew Vaughn.

And, clearly, none of the other names who underwent screen tests was right — and from what I can fathom, Amazon and all concerned panicked. The panic was at such a level that Villeneuve asked to see what Pattinson could do with the From Russia with Love test that all Bond contenders must do.

Passing that test, where actors have to perform a scene from the 1963 film that starred Sean Connery, is bloody hard to pull off. It's a very unnatural environment doing it from that movie.

Look, that's my take. Congrats to Pattinson. I know Villeneuve, who has long dreamed of making a Bond movie, has the cinematic vision to prove me totally wrong about R Patz. After all, he cast him in the new Dune — can't wait to see that!

So, for now, I'll hold off from putting the Curse of Baz upon Bond 26 .

articles.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Players Have Found a New Glitch To Take Advantage of That Wasn't in the Original
articles.summary: Courtesy of Nintendo While many glitches from The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time have been erased in its Switch 2 remake, new ones have arose for players looking for all kinds of exploits. The classic N64 title from 1998 was full of various cheats players used for speed runs, including ways to earn infinite Rupees or even […]
articles.content:
The focus of the new glitch in Ocarina of Time ‘s remake revolves around Gold Skulltula collectibles, special tokens that make up the most extensive side quest in the game. There are 100 Gold Skulltula items in each version of Ocarina of Time , with milestones for each one collected unlocking powerful rewards as your adventure continues. The remake's exploit makes the meticulous hunt for Gold Skulltulas redundant, pairing well with other glitches that trivialize the in-game economy of Ocarina of Time quickly.

The re-designed areas of Hyrule in Ocarina of Time ‘s remake prevents players from utilizing some classic glitches and exploits from the original , including a few fan-favorites. For example, players can't use the drawbridge chains at the Hyrule Castle to walk up them and gain Rupees by jumping off either chain. At the same time, collision physics in areas like Kokiri Forest have been altered so players can't phase through walls to the Great Deku Tree without a sword or shield. Yet, even with all those glitches taken away, players have found a new one close to Hyrule Castle once again.

Once you progress far enough into Ocarina of Time to unlock an older version of Link, you can use Bombs, the Boomerang, and the Song of Storms to reveal a hole near the castle. This automatically grants you at least one Gold Skulltula, unearthing an intended secret in the game. However, by using the Boomerang, players can pick up the Gold Skulltula token originally placed in the area, then do a backflip on a platform used to leave the hole next to the castle. Doing this “resets” the Gold Skulltula to being back in the hole, allowing players to go in, collect it again, and repeat the process as many times as they are able.

This glitch is somewhat hard to execute, as it requires players to have perfect timing with Link's backflip onto a platform used to leave the hole. You almost have to do the flip during the pick-up of the token, so that you aren't revealed to have it with the game's usual fanfare until you are outside of the hole itself. Yet, those who have the skills to manage this even a few times can turn one Gold Skulltula into several, easily reaching one of the game's biggest milestones. Here are just some of the rewards players can get for collecting certain amounts of Gold Skulltula tokens:

The biggest boon from this remake glitch is the last reward given to players for the Gold Skulltulas, given to you at the Skulltula House. The Gold Rupee is essentially a free ticket to buy whatever you want in the game, from extra resources to expensive items at various shops. This makes trading items far easier, especially with the remake's introduction of the Business Scrub Seed, a tool that lets players spawn a shop right next to them. These shops sell useful gear, like Deku Sticks, Bombs, Red Potions, and other great items to flesh out your inventory.

While it's unclear if Nintendo will remove this content in Ocarina of Time ‘s remake, this new glitch is actually one of the best ways the Switch 2 titles is continuing a series tradition. This is yet another speed runner's dream of an exploit, bypassing a barrier to make a new playthrough far, far easier to get through. Even if you mess up the glitch, Gold Skulltulas still exist in the game outside the repeatable one outside Hyrule Castle. Just using the glitch to get to a milestone fast may help out players doing a second or third playthrough of the game, and don't want to tediously hunt for all 100 collectibles again.

Despite all the changes the remake has brought, this exploit shows that the game still shares many traits with the original. Fans will undoubtedly take this highly celebrated remake and find as many exploits as they can, investigating it down to its very code due to how beloved it is by all sorts of players. If anything, this proves that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has a chance to build an equally passionate community as the original had, with new quirks that help it stand out from constant comparisons to the legendary classic.

Though there was talk of an actor potentially replacing Majors in the role, the lackluster reception to Ant-Man and […]
articles.content:
Kevin Feige himself is here to dispute that, though, confirming that Marvel had plans to bring Doctor Doom into the fold even before Majors' legal troubles. Speaking with Empire in the latest issue of the magazine, the Marvel boss revealed that the original plan for Avengers: The Kang Dynasty would have seen Doctor Doom dispatch the title villain and make his MCU debut after all. “ We were changing [ The Kang Dynasty ] even at that point ,” Feige said of Quantumania ‘s poor performance. “It probably would still have been called ‘The Kang Dynasty,' but it would have been a set-up for Doom, midway through that movie.”

Feige has been rather tight-lipped about what happened at Marvel Studios surrounding Jonathan Majors. The actor was arrested in March of 2023 and charged with assault, strangulation, and harassment, and was found guilty in December of that year, with Marvel severing ties soon after.

In their talk with him, Empire noted that Feige was “choosing his words carefully” about the situation, with the Marvel boss noting: “It was very delicate…We didn't want to rush into any rash decisions in terms of employment. People think there was a cause-and-effect with Jonathan's issues, and that certainly accelerated some things. But the Doom of it all was well underway before that.”

Feige went on to admit that the third Ant-Man movie was “not received the way we would have liked” but called out Majors' performance in the film as one of the “many elements” they were proud of from the movie. As fans may recall, Quantumania concluded with a post-credit scene that showed a slew of Kang variants (all played by Majors) that was setting up a collision course for the larger MCU.

Now that we know Marvel was planning to have Doom appear in The Kang Dynasty and dispatch the villain, as set up for a bigger role (presumably in Secret Wars ), it makes the perceived hastiness of Doom in the MCU seem less like a reactionary move than fans have taken it to be.

That said, there's still a perception that Marvel hasn't done enough to set up the threat of Doom himself across the latest phases of their movies and shows, with post-credit teases in The Fantastic Four: First Steps and just last week in VisionQuest being read in an ungenerous manner. We're a month away from the release of Avengers: Doomsday, though, so we'll have our answer on if Marvel did enough before the film's release in just a few weeks.

articles.title: Xbox Reveals New Details on Upcoming Project Helix Console
articles.summary: Xbox has revealed new information on its upcoming Project Helix hardware following its announcement earlier this year. To coincide with the 25th anniversary of the original Xbox's release, the company has been sharing a number of updates and new features that primarily have to do with the history of the brand. As part of looking […]
articles.content:
Shared within a magazine that Xbox recently released, new comments on Project Helix were made by Xbox's Jason Ronald, who is one of the leads spearheading the hardware's creation. Ronald said that Helix is being envisioned as a platform that will be able to seamlessly play games from the entirety of Xbox's history, while also allowing access to PC games as well. When talking about its nature, though, Ronald made clear that Project Helix is an Xbox console first and foremost, and not simply a PC that has been retrofitted to play console games. This distinction is a pretty big one, as it makes clear that Xbox isn't abandoning its own dedicated hardware in favor of a PC-style ecosystem.

“When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine – one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed,” Ronald said. “My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.”

“Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games,” he continued. “The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.”

While these new details on Project Helix continue to heighten interest in the platform, Xbox has yet to say exactly when the hardware will arrive. Past teases from Xbox boss Asha Sharma have indicated that it's currently on track to launch in the holiday season of 2027 , but whether or not this will actually end up happening remains to be seen. As for its price, recent reports have suggested that it could end up selling for as much as $2,000 .

If Project Helix does end up being released in roughly one year, this means that we'll likely end up learning more about this relatively soon. To that end, once we have new info on the release, price, and actual name of Project Helix, we'll be sure to let you know here on ComicBook .

articles.title: The Next Bond Girl: From Zendaya to Florence Pugh, 19 Actresses Who Could Join Robert Pattinson
articles.summary: The name is Pattinson, Robert Pattinson, but who will be his first Bond Girl? Amazon MGM Studios has made it official, naming the 40-year-old Brit the next James Bond in the exclusive franchise, with Denis Villeneuve helming the next film from a script by Steven Knight and Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing. But 007 […]
articles.content:
Few actors have built a stronger case for a license to kill in 2026 than Adria Arjona. The Puerto Rico-born star plays a battle-hardened Army sniper in “Onslaught,” Adam Wingard's A24 actioner, joins James Gunn's DC Universe as Maxima in “Man of Tomorrow” and plays an FBI agent chasing Michael B. Jordan in Amazon MGM's “The Thomas Crown Affair.” That last one is practically an audition for the studio. After proving in “Hit Man” that she can seduce and outwit a leading man in the same scene, she's the femme fatale this franchise has been missing.

Villeneuve has already shown what Emily Blunt can do with a gun. “Sicario” made her FBI agent Kate Macer the moral center of a brutal cartel thriller, and she's heading back into that morally murky world for “Sicario 3.” Add “Edge of Tomorrow,” the “A Quiet Place” films and Steven Spielberg's alien thriller “Disclosure Day” and the Oscar nominee has more genre mileage than almost anyone on this list. Monica Bellucci proved in “Spectre” that a Bond woman doesn't need to be 25. Make Blunt the seasoned MI6 veteran who has watched too many 007s come and go.

Gemma Chan is technically already part of the Bond universe. In the video game “007 First Light,” she plays Dr. Selina Tan, a brilliant academic with a background in psychology and game theory whose role at MI6 is critical in Bond’s journey to earning 00 status. Now make it canon on the big screen. The British star of “Crazy Rich Asians,” “Eternals” and “The Creator” has the cool authority this franchise runs on, whether she’s behind a desk at Vauxhall Cross or across a baccarat table in Macau. She’d make a natural new M or the next Vesper.

Bond has a long history of casting French actors as both seductive allies and adversaries. So who better to bring a fresh French intrigue to 007’s world than Oscar-winning Marion Cotillard? The French star has already mastered seduction and deception in Robert Zemeckis’ spy thriller “Allied,” opposite Brad Pitt and proved she can hold her own in a blockbuster like Christopher Nolan’s “Inception,” starring alongside Leonardo DiCaprio. Cotillard and Robert Pattinson previously missed the chance to share the screen 15 years ago after Cotillard dropped out of “Cosmopolis.” At 51, she would also bring a welcome twist to the franchise’s tradition of casting younger love interests.

Chase Infiniti is named after Nicole Kidman’s “Batman Forever” character, Chase Meridian, so pairing her with the current Bruce Wayne practically writes itself. The case goes deeper than trivia, though. The former kickboxing trainer stood her ground against Leonardo DiCaprio in her film debut, “One Battle After Another” and earned a BAFTA nomination for leading actress along with a Golden Globe nod. She has called performing in a major action film a lifelong dream. Make her a rookie MI6 operative or, better yet, the agent sent to replace him.

A “Downton Abbey” alum, James has credits across film, TV and theater and playing a Bond Girl would be the major career breakthrough to skyrocket her career. She has shown off her singing chops in “Cinderella” and “Mamma Mia 2,” warmed hearts as love interests in “Baby Driver” and “Yesterday,” then subsequently broke those hearts in “The Iron Claw.” James Bond would be her first big-budget franchise, and James seems ready for it.

Gugu Mbatha-Raw has done British espionage before, with early guest spots on the BBC’s spy drama “Spooks.” Since then, the Oxford-born actor has shown she can play intellect and menace with equal conviction. Her credits include the title role in “Belle,” in addition to the TVA villain Ravonna Renslayer in Disney+’s Marvel series “Loki” and Apple TV’s psychological thriller “Surface,” which she also produced. Imagine that poise turned against 007.

Just like Pattinson started out with “Harry Potter” and “Twilight,” Merced had her Hollywood coming-of-age in movies like “Transformers” and “Dora the Explorer.” Then she started kicking xenomorph ass in “Alien: Romulus” and killing clickers in “The Last of Us.” Most recently, she debuted as the high-flying, mace-wielding hero Hawkgirl in “Superman” and she’ll be back in next year’s “Man of Tomorrow.” Though she’s 15 years younger than Pattinson, Merced’s star is on the rise and she has experience from several major franchises.

Every Bond era needs a discovery, and Inde Navarrette is the breakout of the year. She spent years working on The CW’s superhero drama “Superman & Lois” and Netflix’s teen drama “13 Reasons Why,” then turned the horror hit “Obsession” into a star-making showcase. Hollywood noticed. She has since landed the role of Rogue in Marvel’s “X-Men,” and she’ll star in and executive produce Apple’s sci-fi thriller “The Waffle House Index.” Cast her as a young field agent with something to prove, and she could do for this era what Léa Seydoux did for Daniel Craig’s.

Lupita Nyong'o was already in an epic with Pattinson earlier this year with “The Odyssey.” The Oscar-winning actress from “12 Years a Slave” (2013) also has spy experience. Her Nakia in “Black Panther” is a Wakandan undercover operative, and in “The 355″ she played a former MI6 computer specialist. She deserves a Bond role with that same double edge as an ally whose loyalty 007 the audience can never quite read.

Pugh has fight choreography down after playing Black Widow Yelena Belova in the Marvel Cinematic Universe across several movies, so she could go toe-to-toe with Bond. Playing a Bond girl who can hold her own in a fight with a supervillain’s henchmen seems like a perfect role for Pugh. And she’ll share the screen with Pattinson in “Dune: Part 3,” so they already have a head start on their chemistry.

Qualley put herself on the Bond map when she danced on stage at the Academy Awards for the telecast’s tribute to the franchise in 2025. Just watching her performance, clad in a bright red dress with tuxedoed men, it was impossible not to imagine her tangoing with Bond or waltzing at a black-tie gala in a 007 movie. A trained dancer, Qualley will show off her moves as Adele Astaire in the Fred Astaire biopic and she’ll get a taste of the spy life in next year’s “Possession” remake.

Margot Robbie has already played the con artist in “Focus,” the scene-stealer in “The Wolf of Wall Street” and the agent of chaos Harley Quinn. A Bond film would be the logical next heist. She’s fresh off playing Catherine Earnshaw opposite Jacob Elordi’s Heathcliff in “Wuthering Heights.” An untitled “Ocean’s Eleven” prequel is in development with her name attached, so she’s clearly in a caper state of mind. Picture her as a high-society villain with a twinkle in her eye and a blade in her clutch.

Sam Mendes directed “Skyfall” and “Spectre,” and he’s now cast Anna Sawai as Yoko Ono in his Beatles films. On FX’s historical drama “Shōgun,” she became the first Japanese actress to win the Emmy for lead drama actress but her action credentials go back to “Ninja Assassin” and “F9.” Sawai can convey loyalty and menace along with some heartbreak in a single look. Isn’t that the entire job description of a great Bond woman?

Not only would Hunter Schafer make history as the first trans Bond girl, she’d be a damn good one. Schafer has proven her acting skills over and over in “Euphoria” and is about to level up as one of the stars of the “Blade Runner 2099” series, which will undoubtedly have some intense action scenes. Yet she’s still at the phase where scoring a Bond role could completely catapult her career. We could totally see Schafer and Pattinson sharing flirty banter before going head-to-head against some baddies — and just imagine the looks on that press tour!

As a blonde bombshell, Sydney Sweeney would be a Bond Girl no-brainer — and she just might have the action chops to match. Sweeney is a natural athlete — she trained for months and put on 30 pounds to play a fierce boxer in “Christy” — but still hasn’t starred in a true action movie unless you count Marvel flop “Madame Web.” This could be the perfect chance for her to flex that muscle. It remains to be seen if she could match Pattinson’s zany personality — but with her Jeff Bezos connection (Sweeney attended his wedding last year and he invested in her lingerie brand), she’s likely to be at the top of Amazon’s list.

Like Pugh, Taylor-Joy is another “Dune: Part 3” leading lady who is sure to attract some Bond Girl fan castings after people see her starring alongside Pattinson. She’s had some stunt training after starring as Imperator Furiosa in the “Mad Max: Fury Road” prequel, and she’ll anchor a major franchise next year with “The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum.” And who wouldn’t want a high-stakes chess showdown between her and Bond, calling back to her “Queen’s Gambit” breakout role?

Turner is already a major TV star thanks to “Game of Thrones,” but that hasn’t quite translated to the big screen. Playing a Bond Girl could change all that. She’s proven she can deliver a wordy monologue and give an icy stare after surviving Westeros politics in “Game of Thrones,” and she’s trained extensively to star in Prime Video’s “Tomb Raider” series as explorer Lara Croft. The Amazon MGM connection between the series and Bond is already there, giving Turner an easy jump to the spy world.

Nobody has spent more screen time with Robert Pattinson this year than Zendaya. They played Emma and Charlie, an engaged couple, in A24’s “The Drama” before reuniting in Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey,” where Zendaya plays Athena. By the end of the year, they’ll be together with the future 007 auteur Denis Villeneuve in his epic conclusion, “Dune: Part Three.” With three films of proven chemistry, plus a director who already knows how to make her the most magnetic presence on a desert-swept screen, give her a morally slippery MI6 asset who’s never fully on Bond’s side and let the two-time Emmy winner keep everyone guessing.

articles.title: Should Spider-Man: Brand New Day Get An Oscar Nom For Best Picture? A Sony Exec Makes The Case
articles.summary: Conquering the box office may have only been the beginning.
articles.content:
I knew Spider-Man: Brand New Day would make a ridiculous amount of money when it landed on this summer's 2026 movie schedule . What I didn't expect was to hear Sony's top movie executive making a serious case for Tom Holland 's latest superhero adventure to earn a Best Picture Oscar nomination. But here we are, and apparently, the studio is prepared to put some real effort into making it happen.

I actually get what he's saying. While I enjoyed the action in Brand New Day , what stuck with me was how much of the movie focused on Peter's loneliness after the events of No Way Home . Here's a guy who can swing between skyscrapers and take down some of Marvel's most dangerous villains , but he can't get the people he loves to remember who he is. That's a pretty miserable situation, even by Peter Parker standards.

Sony is backing up those comments with an actual campaign. According to Deadline , the studio has hired awards consultants and is planning special screenings and filmmaker Q&As beginning ahead of Thanksgiving. There's also talk of a theatrical rerelease designed to put the movie back in front of audiences and Academy voters.

As for Spider-Man, the character, he hasn't exactly been an Academy favorite. Sam Raimi's Spider-Man 2 won Best Visual Effects in 2005, while Into the Spider-Verse took home Best Animated Feature in 2019. Although no movie starring the web-slinger has ever competed for Best Picture.

As a trained actor who left L.A. for a Texas ranch, how did Hollywood pull you back for this show?

This experience was truly one of the most exciting acting experiences of my life. When you're on a set, you show up to play a character, but then when the director says “cut,” you go back to being Ben. When you're playing Traitors , the director never says cut. You are in character at all times. Even when the cameras are not rolling, you still have to play whatever character you're showing up as. If you're having lunch, you can never break character. You have to play it up the whole time.

I have a pretty large and loud personality, so I really had to tone it back, which was challenging because I want to be the center of attention. I wanna go be loud, but that's immediately going to put a target on my back. I also didn't tell anyone that I was an actor. I really leaned in to, “I'm this gay cowboy," which is not a lie. I really am the gay cowboy. It's just that the gay cowboy is more of a hobby than my career.

The producers hired me to play a game about lying and deceit. But the show is non-union, so there are definitely people there who aren't trying to pursue an acting or Hollywood career. For instance, Abby L. didn't even have Instagram before she got on the show. She's an astrophysicist, so she must be a fan of the show and then applied. There are people from all different walks of life, which was amazing.

Were you a fan of The Traitors ?

I went to BravoCon and saw this Traitors thing, and I remember asking my friend, "What is Traitors ?" She was like, "You don't watch Traitors ?" I had never seen it. She's like, "You have to watch. It's the best show." I was like, whatever. Then in Texas, we got an insane ice storm last January and here in Texas, when you get an ice storm, you're stuck at home because no one knows how to drive. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

AJ, my husband, came out one day like, "What are you watching?” I'm like, "Let's just watch this Traitors thing." I turn on one episode — instantly hooked. I binged every season of the U.K. show, every season of the U.S. show. Then two weeks later I got the phone call: "Would you be interested in The Traitors ?" I was like, "I just binged it. This is crazy."

Next thing you know, I'm at a Scottish castle with Alan Cumming, playing Clue , basically, in the middle of the Scottish Highlands.

Were you pursuing acting at the time? Or do you feel like it was lucky timing?

Acting has always been my main goal. As an actor, I never thought I would do reality TV. For a long time, I was opposed. I've had other offers in life for a reality show idea, and I've always been like, "You can't do reality and be taken seriously as an actor." I do feel there has been a shift. Like, 10 years ago when I was like, "I can't be gay and be an actor because I'm going to be put in this box where you're just the gay actor." That is totally not the case anymore. You can be gay and play straight roles, you can be straight and play gay roles. It's not as scary as it used to be.

So same thing with reality. You you look at people like our Ariana Madix from Vanderpump Rules . She's on Broadway. She's on an NBC show. She's doing all sorts of stuff. There are so many different reality stars who are now pursuing scripted. So I guess it was not quite as scary, but scripted television and movies have always been number one. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I know you were hoping to be a Traitor. What was your strategy going in? And did your strategy change once you found out you were a Faithful?

I had only thought about being a Traitor. It was so set in my mind.. There was absolutely no question of me not being a Traitor. Stupidly, that did not even enter my brain. Preparing for the show, flying over there in the castle. At no point was I like, "What am I going to do if I'm a Faithful?"

So when I didn't feel the tap on my shoulder, I remember being like, "Do I need to ask someone if didn't feel the tap? Like, for sure, I'm a Traitor." And when I was a Faithful, I laid in bed that night and was like, "Well, now what?"

If you're a Traitor, it's strategy all the way. You need to plan. You need to think 10 steps ahead. If you're a Faithful, it's a popularity contest. We are back in high school, and you need the Traitors to think you trust them so they want to keep you around, and you need the Faithful to like you so that they don't banish you. You can watch every season of every Traitors in every different country. What you think would work with one group of people may not work with the next. You have no idea how different people will react.

Personally, I think my training at The Groundlings and with improv really helped me roll with the punches. You had to go with it. I really didn't try to overthink it. Once I was a Faithful, I'm like, "Just be honest." And it got me quite far.

This is a huge thing to keep secret from family, friends, work. What was that like for you? Did you tell anyone? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

AJ is the only person I told. When you go to Scotland to film, you have no phone. No internet. No connection to the outside world. I was gone during my birthday. It's very overwhelming.

I actually thought I was going to miss not having my phone. It was so nice and relaxing to not have a phone. The only thing that would drive me nuts is wondering, "Who's trying to contact me?" I was like, "People are going to think I'm going to rehab." ( Laughs .)

I'm very active on social media. I post on my story all the time. The fact that I've just gone completely quiet? Also, I had to record my podcast, It's Ben a Week , in advance. I had to get all the social media clips. So my podcast Instagram posted a clip every single day. But I was like, "What if I'm causing drama and I'm not even responding?" You have no control.

Let's go inside your elimination. You were very calm. What did you mean when you said, "I knew it was time" before you opened the envelope and found out you were murdered?

I'm one of the calmest people I know. Nothing riles me up that much. I'm always like, "It's fine." That's my line. This show caused so much anxiety! I've never had anxiety. I'm like, "Can someone get me a Xanax, please? ( Laughs .) Because I think I need one."

So every morning I would wake up freaking out. And for some reason, the day I got murdered, I was so calm. That morning I actually started packing my things. I knew there was something coming. That fur coat that I wore? I brought that to wear either at the finale or when I'm murdered. I even talked about with the stylist about saving that coat, and that day, I brought the coat with me. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

When I opened the door, I saw the envelope and there was a little hint of me that was like, "Maybe I'm being recruited [to be a Traitor,]" which I was like, "What a dream." And then I was like, I don't think so. That's when I was like, it was time. I was ready to go.

What's the exit process like? Do you leave right after that?

You do more confessionals. You're there for a whole other day doing stuff. But you don't get to say goodbye to anyone. Shooting the show is such an immersive experience that you have to remind yourself no one is dying. They don't waste money on budget or any of the production value. That funeral scene, for example, when we were in the graveyard and there was smoke and fog and you see a gravestone with your name on it? You're watching your friends get into coffins in the ground. It feels real. Then the exits are abrupt; no goodbyes. It's like, boom, gone.
